prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a layered layout: nearby ground and vegetation occupy the bright lower foreground, the deer is several metres ahead (roughly 3–6 m), and the darker tree line and field extend farther behind it. Across the five frames, the deer remains in front of the camera wearer and shifts from left-of-centre toward the right, while its similar apparent depth suggests mostly lateral movement rather than a strong approach or retreat; no people are visible. The deer is well beyond the camera wearer’s arm’s reach, and no other animal is close enough to assess animal-to-animal spacing. Compared with RGB, the map makes foreground–background separation and the deer’s full silhouette clearer, but its saturated brightness, unstable tree/sky boundaries, and similarly bright foreground foliage make metric distance and partial occlusions unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates one deer against the scene, showing it moving from the left side through the centre toward the right across the five frames; the fourth-frame detection is missing even though the deer remains visible in RGB. Its mask indicates the deer is fully ahead of the camera wearer, several metres away (roughly 3–6 m), with no segmented people or additional objects from which to estimate pairwise distances or arm’s reach. The silhouettes clarify the deer’s position and orientation despite the dark, cluttered ground: it is broadly side-on and progresses to the right, with some leg shapes overlapping or merging. The map is unreliable in class identity—labeling the same deer first as “cow” and later as “dog”—and it removes all scene layout, depth, vegetation occlusions, and background objects.
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains yellow skeletal detections only in the first two frames, positioned over the deer on the left and then near the centre-left; there are no magenta hand detections and no actual people visible in RGB. Because these skeletons are false body-pose fits to an animal, they do not reliably establish human facing direction, gaze toward the camera wearer, limb reach, or interpersonal distance. Their movement roughly follows the deer’s left-to-right image motion, but the absence of detections in frames three through five prevents a dependable account of approach, retreat, or turning. The map could normally expose articulated body geometry that RGB obscures, yet here its malformed joints, animal alignment, and dropped later frames make that spatial information unreliable.
